question: What is the penalty for using the ISI mark without a licence?
answer:
**Short answer**: Using the Standard Mark (ISI mark) without a licence is a contravention of section 17, and the offender is punishable under Section 29(3) of the BIS Act, 2016 [1].

**Details**:
The offence of contravening section 17 is cognizable [1].

**Step-by-step**:
1. If convicted for the first contravention, the person shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term up to two years, or with a fine not less than two lakh rupees, or both [1].
2. For the second and subsequent contraventions, the fine shall not be less than five lakh rupees [1].
3. The fine may extend up to ten times the value of goods or articles produced or sold or offered to be sold or affixed or applied with a Standard Mark, including Hallmark [1].
4. Where the value of the goods or articles cannot be determined, it is presumed that one year's production was in contravention, and the annual turnover in the previous financial year is taken as the value of the goods [1].

**Official links**:
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in
- BIS CARE app: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bis.bisapp

**Sources:**
[1] Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016: CHAPTER V > Section 29(3) Penalty for contravention, p. 14, dated 2016-03-22 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/BIS-Act-2016.pdf#page=14
expected: Section 29(3) of the BIS Act, 2016: contravening Section 17 is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine of not less than two lakh rupees for the first contravention and not less than five lakh rupees for subsequent contraventions, which may extend up to ten times the value of goods, or both.

answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, you can still apply for renewal within 90 days from the last date of validity by paying the requisite fee along with a late fee of ₹ 5,000 [1]. If the renewal application and fee are not received within this 90-day period, the licence shall stand expired [1][2].

**Details**:
- **Deferment period**: If the renewal application with the requisite fee is not received before the expiration of validity, the decision to renew may be deferred for up to 90 days from the validity date [2].
- **Late fee requirement**: Making the renewal application after the licence validity requires an accompanying late fee of rupees five thousand [2].
- **Status of marking**: You have no right to mark the product with the standard mark after the date of validity [1].
- **Consequences of non-application**: If the renewal application and requisite fee (including late fee) are not received within 90 days, the licence shall stand expired [1][2].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Submit the renewal application form along with the requisite fee and a late fee of ₹ 5,000 [1].
2. Ensure this submission happens within 90 days from the last date of validity [1].
3. Provide an undertaking that future renewal applications will be submitted to BIS before the validity date (if renewed within the deferment period) [1].

**Official links**:
- Manak Online: https://www.manakonline.in/
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in

**Sources:**
[1] Guidelines for Renewal of Licence: 2., p. 1, dated 2025-03-05 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/RenewalGuidelines-WebsiteHosting.pdf#page=1
[2] BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018: p. 2, dated 2018 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/BIS_CA_12032019.pdf#page=2
expected: Yes, within 90 days after the validity date, by paying an additional late fee of ₹5,000; the decision to renew may be deferred for up to 90 days from the validity date.

question: Is BIS certification compulsory for Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, BIS certification is compulsory for Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement.

**Details**:
*   Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement is listed under **Scheme I (ISI mark)** for products under compulsory certification [1].
*   It falls under the category of "Cement (any variety of cement manufactured or sold in India)" [1].
*   The product is governed by the **Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003** (S.O. No. 191(E) Dt. 17 Feb 2003) [1].
*   The specific Indian Standard for this product is **IS 12330** [1].

**Official links**:
*   BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in
*   Manak Online (apply for / manage a licence): https://www.manakonline.in/

**Sources:**
[1] Scheme I (ISI mark): products under compulsory certification: IS 12330: Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-1/?lang=en
expected: Yes, IS 12330 under Scheme I (ISI mark), Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003, S.O. 191(E) dated 17 Feb 2003.

question: Do electronic control gears for LED modules need CRS registration?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, DC or AC supplied electronic control gear for LED modules requires CRS registration under Scheme II.

**Details**:
*   **Product**: DC or AC Supplied Electronic Control gear for LED Modules.
*   **Scheme**: Scheme II (CRS registration) [1].
*   **Regulatory Basis**: The requirement is governed by the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021, along with its amendments (S.O.1246 (E) Dated 10 March, 2026) [1].

**Official links**:
*   CRS registration portal: https://www.crsbis.in/BIS/registration-page.do

**Sources:**

question: बिना लाइसेंस के ISI मार्क लगाने पर क्या सज़ा है?
answer:
**Short answer**: बिना लाइसेंस के ISI मार्क (Standard Mark) लगाने पर सेक्शन 17 का उल्लंघन माना जाता है, जिसके लिए BIS अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 29(3) के तहत सजा का प्रावधान है [1][2]。

**Details**:
- यह अपराध संज्ञेय (cognizable) होता है [2]।
- यदि मूल्य निर्धारित नहीं किया जा सकता, तो पिछले वित्तीय वर्ष के वार्षिक कारोबार को उत्पादन का मूल्य माना जाएगा [2]।

**सज़ा (Penalty)**:
- पहली बार उल्लंघन करने पर दो साल तक की कैद या कम से कम दो लाख रुपये का जुर्माना (जो उत्पादित, बेचे गए या ऑफर किए गए सामान के मूल्य का दस गुना तक हो सकता है), या दोनों [2]।
- दूसरे और उसके बाद के उल्लंघनों के लिए कम से कम पाँच लाख रुपये का जुर्माना, या दो साल तक की कैद, या दोनों [2]।

**Official links**:
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in
- BIS CARE app (verify licence, HUID, CRS R-number; complaints): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bis.bisapp

**स्रोत:**
[1] Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016: CHAPTER V > Section 29(2) Penalty for contravention, p. 13, dated 2016-03-22 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/BIS-Act-2016.pdf#page=13
[2] Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016: CHAPTER V > Section 29(3) Penalty for contravention, p. 14, dated 2016-03-22 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/BIS-Act-2016.pdf#page=14
expected: Section 29(3): imprisonment up to two years, fine at least 2 lakh (first) / 5 lakh (subsequent), up to ten times value of goods.
